This week: seed libraries, a heron and a question about mulch.
View in browser

Hello again,

October is the month when the garden starts handing things back. The beans are finished, the tomatoes are down to a few green stragglers on the windowsill, and the compost heap is taller than it has been all year. It is also, it turns out, the busiest month for the seed library at the end of my road.

The seed library

It lives in an old card catalogue in the community centre. You take a packet, grow the plants, and bring back seeds from the best of them at the end of the season. This year the drawer marked Beans, climbing came back fuller than it went out.

A visitor

A grey heron has started standing on my neighbour's shed roof every morning, staring at the pond with enormous patience. The pond has no fish in it. I have not had the heart to tell the heron.

Your questions

Several of you asked whether it is too late to mulch. It is not. A thick layer of leaves or compost spread now will protect the soil over winter and feed it slowly; just keep it a hand's width away from the stems of shrubs.

Until next month,
Nadia
